selection_reasoning: These 4 tasks form a coherent multi-hop sequence centered around building a decorated house. The player must first find a wolf (to serve as a pet/guard for the house), find pink_glazed_terracotta (decorative building material), and craft a block of redstone (for functional redstone components in the house). All three of these tasks feed into the final 'Build a house' task, which incorporates the gathered materials and the wolf as a companion. The wolf-finding and terracotta-finding tasks are parallel prerequisites, while the redstone block crafting is another parallel prerequisite. This creates a fan-in DAG structure where three tasks converge into the final building task.

edges.reason: The wolf must be found and tamed first to serve as the house's guard companion
Pink glazed terracotta is needed as decorative wall material for the house interior
Redstone block is needed for powering redstone lamp lighting inside the house

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task. The wolves are placed at spawn-relative (8, 0, 8) with NoAI so they stay put. The player must navigate within 5 blocks and face the wolf's direction (facing_tolerance=60°) to demonstrate they have visually located it. This is the preferred rule for find/observe tasks.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task. The pink glazed terracotta cluster is at spawn-relative (-5, 0, -5). The player must navigate within 5 blocks and face the terracotta (facing_tolerance=60°) to demonstrate visual discovery. This is the preferred rule for find/observe tasks.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a block of redstone (9 redstone dust → 1 redstone_block at the crafting table) results in the item appearing in the player's inventory. The player starts with 128 redstone dust and 0 redstone blocks, so having ≥1 redstone_block confirms successful crafting. This is the preferred rule for craft tasks.

Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind='block') because building/furnishing a house requires placing blocks inside it. The pre-built oak frame occupies spawn-relative (10-14, 0-5, 10-14) with interior space at (11-13, 1-3, 11-13). Checking for a redstone_lamp placed within the house walls (box [10,1,10] to [14,5,14]) confirms the player has actively furnished the interior. The redstone lamp requires the previously crafted redstone_block to power it, enforcing the craft dependency. Box matches the actual house structure boundaries exactly.

scene_description: A flat grass field scene with: (1) Two wolves at +8,+8 for finding/taming, (2) Pink glazed terracotta blocks at -5,-5 for discovery, (3) A crafting table at -8,+3 for crafting redstone blocks, (4) A pre-built oak house frame at +10-14,+10-14 that serves as the house-building target. Player inventory contains redstone, bones, oak planks, doors, glass panes, torches, and redstone lamps.
task_text: Complete the following tasks: 1) Find a wolf nearby and tame it with bones. 2) Find the pink glazed terracotta blocks. 3) Use the crafting table to craft a block of redstone from your redstone dust. 4) Build/furnish a house using the provided materials, incorporating the redstone block and pink terracotta as decoration.
design_notes: Player spawns at center facing south. Wolves are NE at +8,+8 (NoAI so they stay put). Pink terracotta is SW at -5,-5. Crafting table is at -8,+3 (west). House frame is at +10-14,+10-14 (NE corner) with a 2-block doorway facing the player. The scene is compact (~30x30 blocks) with all objectives within 20 blocks of spawn. The house has walls, floor, roof, and a door opening - player can furnish/decorate it.
